source.title: Stable Language Model Pre-training by Reducing Embedding Variability
source.authors: Woo-Jin Chung; Jiwoo Hong; Na-Min An; James Thorne; SeYoung Yun

record.tranche_reason: The study varies model depth and reports zero-shot perplexity on several datasets, bearing conceptually on whether downstream performance improves with scale. It does not fit or test scaling-law predictions.
record.gate_note: The paper cites scaling-law work but does not test power-law loss, extrapolation from small runs, or compute-optimal allocation. Its TEV and gradient-variance results concern pre-training stability, not a claim version. Rows record the separately reported zero-shot perplexities across depth and dataset.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates a stability proxy and a proposed attention architecture. Its depth sweep shows decreasing zero-shot perplexity, but does not establish downstream predictability with scale or pretraining loss. It reports no power-law fits, extrapolation tests, compute-optimal allocation, or depth/width sweep at fixed parameter count. Comparisons of MLRA with baselines report the proposed method's performance rather than test a scaling law.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors' conclusion: TEV is proposed as an efficient stability proxy, and MLRA reduces gradient explosion, TEV, and generally zero-shot perplexity, especially in deeper models. Their broad superiority statement has a Table 1 exception: at 192 layers on WIKI103, MLRA scores 44.17 versus σReparam's 44.13.
record.recipe_differences: This is a stability and architecture study: GPT-2 variants are trained from scratch with MLRA or σReparam and evaluated by zero-shot perplexity; it does not reproduce a scaling-law fit.
record.method_sensitivity: Depth (48, 96, and 192 layers) and architecture method (GPT-2, σReparam, MLRA) vary across the reported results.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 1 perplexity decreases from 48 to 96 to 192 layers for each method on all five datasets, without a predictive scaling relationship being tested.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing depth improves zero-shot language-model perplexity in these reported WebText-trained configurations.

fits_no_version.finding: MLRA generally improves zero-shot perplexity against the baselines under the authors' matched training configurations; the 192-layer WIKI103 comparison with σReparam is an exception.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Factorized attention can improve stability and zero-shot perplexity in the tested GPT-2 configurations.

fits_no_version.finding: Figures 1–3 examine embedding variability, gradient variance, and training failures rather than scaling-law loss or downstream predictability.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Token embedding variability tracks training instability, and MLRA reduces gradient variance.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The authors state that their controlled pre-training study is limited to a maximum of 1.5B parameters and one corpus, WebText. The perplexity results are reported for three depths and do not establish a fitted prediction or extrapolation.

untested.parts: Power-law dependence of held-out pretraining loss on parameters, tokens, or compute over orders of magnitude.
Prediction of larger-run loss using fits to small runs.
Compute-optimal parameter/token allocation and its scaling exponents.
Loss sensitivity across a wide range of depth/width configurations at fixed parameter count; the depth sweep holds hidden dimension fixed and changes parameter count.
Power-law form in other modalities or training regimes; four-epoch training alone does not test a repeated-data scaling law.
Predictable downstream performance as a function of scale or pretraining loss; monotonic perplexity across three depths is insufficient.
Dependence of fitted exponents or compute-optimal splits on setup and fitting choices, or departures from a single power law.

record.verdict_notes: Section 4.1 states parameter counts are fixed across methods, but this is a comparison of the proposed method with baselines, not a wide fixed-parameter shape sweep. All 45 perplexity values match Table 1. The cannot_determine states concern the claimed scaling effect, not the readability of those values. No commands, files, or external sources were accessed.

versions.untested_parts: Power-law loss against parameters, tokens, or compute.
Prediction of larger-run loss from fits to smaller runs.
Architecture comparisons at fixed parameter count.
The study reports perplexity across three depths, but does not fit a predictive relationship, report parameter counts for those runs, or relate downstream performance to pre-training loss.
Dependence of scaling-law exponents or compute-optimal allocation on setup or fitting choices.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Perplexity across 48-, 96-, and 192-layer runs for GPT-2, σReparam, and MLRA on the five reported datasets
reader_labels.reason: Perplexity decreases with depth for each method on each listed dataset; see rows r1–r45. This supports improvement across the tested depth sweep, not a fitted or extrapolative prediction.
